title: The else if Statement knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the most direct learning goal for this lesson?
options: The main goal is to apply multiple alternative conditions in a small Swift example and verify the result.
Use the else if statement only for visual styling.
Skip type checking and accept any result.
Replace a focused example with unrelated code.
questions.answer_key: The main goal is to apply multiple alternative conditions in a small Swift example and verify the result.
questions.explanation: The else if Statement is best learned through a small, verifiable example. Build a minimal example for multiple alternative conditions, then inspect both the source and its result. Keep values and control flow explicit so the compiler and a reader can verify the intended behavior.

questions.prompt: Which practice supports maintainable Swift code?
options: Force all values through unsafe operations.
Ignore ownership and errors when an example works once.
Use the newest API without checking target compatibility.
Use documented Swift semantics, explicit data flow and a test for a meaningful edge case.
questions.answer_key: Use documented Swift semantics, explicit data flow and a test for a meaningful edge case.
